facts.statement: The genus Serpianosaurus was described by Rieppel in 1989.
Serpianosaurus, meaning "Serpiano lizard", lived during the Middle Triassic in Switzerland and Germany.
facts.quote: Serpianosaurus (meaning "Serpiano lizard") is an extinct genus of pachypleurosaurs known from the Middle Triassic (late Anisian and early Ladinian stages) deposits of Switzerland and Germany.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Serpianosaurus mirigiolensis was a small reptile measuring 75 cm in length.
facts.quote: It was a small reptile, with the type specimen of S. mirigiolensis measuring 75 cm long.

facts.statement: Fossils of Serpianosaurus mirigiolensis date to around 242 million years ago at the Anisian/Ladinian boundary.
facts.quote: The locality dates back to sometime around the Anisian/Ladinian boundary of the Middle Triassic, around 242 Ma

facts.statement: Morphological evidence suggests Serpianosaurus is one of the most basal forms of sauropterygians.
facts.quote: Certain aspects of its morphology also suggest it is one of the most basal forms.

facts.statement: A second species, Serpianosaurus germanicus, was described and named by Cajus G. Diedrich in 2013.
facts.quote: In 2013, Cajus G. Diedrich described and named a second species of the genus, S. germanicus

facts.statement: Serpianosaurus germanicus dates to the late Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic.
facts.quote: This species represents the oldest well-known record of this genus, as it comes from the upper Pelsonian, dating to the late Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic.

facts.statement: Sexual dimorphism in Serpianosaurus is indicated by differences in humeral size and shape between males and females.
facts.quote: Like many other pachypleurosaurs, sexual dimorphism can be seen in Serpianosaurus. Males and females are thought to differ in humeral size and shape.

facts.statement: Specimens of Serpianosaurus lack pachyostosis in their ribs.
facts.quote: Any pachyostosis of the ribs is absent in Serpianosaurus specimens.

facts.statement: Serpianosaurus belongs to the superorder Sauropterygia.
Serpianosaurus is classified within the family Pachypleurosauridae.
The genus Serpianosaurus was established by Rieppel in 1989.
Fossils of Serpianosaurus have been found in the middle Grenzbitumenzone, the oldest strata of Monte San Giorgio in Switzerland.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles se han hallado en la zona media de Grenzbitumenzone, los estratos más antiguos del Monte San Giorgio, Suiza

facts.statement: The locality where Serpianosaurus fossils were found dates to near the Anisian/Ladinian boundary, approximately 237 million years ago.
facts.quote: La localidad data de cerca del límite entre el Anisiense y el Ladiniense en el Triásico Medio, hace cerca de 237 millones de años

facts.statement: Certain aspects of Serpianosaurus morphology suggest it is one of the most basal forms.
facts.quote: Ciertos aspectos de su morfología también sugieren que es una de las formas más basales.

facts.statement: No pachyostosis has been found in the ribs of Serpianosaurus specimens.
facts.quote: No se ha hallado paquiostosis en las costillas de los especímenes de Serpianosaurus.

facts.statement: The parent group of Serpianosaurus is Pachypleurosauridae.
The type species of Serpianosaurus is Serpianosaurus mirigiolensis.
There are 14 recorded fossil occurrences of Serpianosaurus.
